recommendation: Keep the audit commit. No core follow-up is needed unless a future final work group decision brings Permission back into core; future Permission activity actor changes belong in HL7/data-access-policies.
issue_request: Applied/Persuasive Security issue asking for Permission activity actors to identify actors by role, mirroring Consent.provision.actor with role and reference so policies can apply to anyone asserting a functional or structural role.
initial_application: No commit found in history mentions FHIR-45077 directly. Commit 888dcbab3ac68f2ed5098d0f16e2962a5fbb8e1b, 'Permission needs and activity role code', appears to apply the issue by adding Permission.rule.activity.actor.role and Permission.rule.activity.actor.reference in source/permission/structuredefinition-Permission.xml with Consent.provision.actor mappings.
additional_context: Commit 0e2a8a7f839d5e1a43787523daccf07d958362f3 later removed Permission from core by deleting source/permission and active fhir.ini Permission entries. The current Security module links Permission to the HL7 Data Access Policies IG, and that external StructureDefinition still contains Permission.rule.activity.actor.role with the participation-role-type binding.
reconciliation: Published an empty external-repo audit commit on the combined branch. No core source was changed because reintroducing Permission would conflict with the later removal from the current core build, while the requested role capability is preserved externally.

related_jiras.note: Another applied Permission issue already audited on the combined branch with the same later external-repo scope finding.
